messages:
Anya: Heads-up — we had a 15m 429 spike for several orgs around 10:12 UTC. Dashboards show per-key rates flat but per-org buckets exhausted. Not noise from a single client.
Sam: Ugh. Any obvious root cause yet? rollout? changes to burst window?
Anya: No deploys at that time. Looks like traffic pattern changed — sustained small bursts from many keys that add up against per-org burst allowance.
Luc: Can you paste the grafana panel or query? I want to see the token-bucket levels.
Anya: Pasting the panel query we used in Grafana (Prometheus):
```promql
sum by (org_id) (rate(rate_limiter_rejected_total{reason="burst_exhausted"}[5m]))
```
Also a derived metric of current burst_credit per org:
```promql
avg by (org_id) (rate_limiter_burst_credit{env="prod"})
```
Maria: Current alerts are only on global 429 rate and per-key qps. We never alerted on per-org burst credit falling below threshold.
Sam: We should add a per-org alert and a CS runbook entry. For alerting, propose: trigger when organization has >50 429s in 5m AND burst_credit < 10 for 3m.
Luc: Suggest also a heavy tail check: if top-10 orgs account for >60% of 429s spike, notify infra+customers. Use this query in Datadog/Grafana as a ratio.
Anya: Draft of the Datadog monitor expression I tested:
```
(sum:rate_limiter.rejected{env:prod,reason:burst_exhausted}.rollup(sum, 300)) by {org_id} > 50
AND
(avg:rate_limiter.burst_credit{env:prod}.rollup(avg, 180)) by {org_id} < 10
```
Sam: Good. What escalation path? Pager to eng-sre for production-facing incidents, alert to cs with low urgency first so CS can preemptively reach out.
Maria: For CS runbook: 1) check per-org dashboard panel, 2) check recent deploys & routing rules, 3) if persistent, propose temporary per-org burst increase or throttle tuning, 4) open ticket with account and engineering.
cs-bot: Suggested template for CS outreach:
"We observed elevated request throttling for your account between 10:12–10:27 UTC. We can coordinate temporary burst adjustments or recommend rate shaping — please reply with your expected sustained qps."
Luc: Edge case: don't auto-increase bursts without consent for paid customers. Instead offer a 1hr manual bump via the console flag behind audit log.
Anya: Action items:
- Luc -> add Grafana panel for per-org burst_credit (done as temp panel)
- Sam -> create Datadog monitor with the expression above (prio P1 for monitoring)
- Maria -> add CS runbook steps and outreach template to ops playbook
- Anya -> add a short console UX note: show 'burst remaining' on the quota card
Sam: I'll create the monitor and link it here.
Luc: I'll add the Grafana panel and a csv export for the last 7 days of bursts for the oncall.
Anya: Thx. Also let's add a dashboard row showing fallback routing counts (how many requests were routed to cheaper model after 429) — helps understand graceful degradation.
pagerbot: Deploy scheduled: grafana/dashboard/per-org-burst -> staging at 1749130000, prod at 1749133600
Maria: Once monitors are live, I'll run a quick tabletop test with CS and oncall next week to validate alerts and templates.
Anya: Great. If anyone sees similar spikes overnight, drop a message here with org IDs so we can correlate.
